speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction and how long it has been going on? Also, have you noticed any other unusual bleeding or bruising in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: The bleeding from my gums hasn't stopped even after using several gauze packs, and it's been going on for a while now. I also bruise very easily, and my uncle has had similar bleeding issues and joint swelling in the past. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling and easy bruising, I suspect a clotting factor deficiency like Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel (PT, PTT, Factor VIII and IX levels)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec; Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT): 60 sec; Bleeding Time: 6 min; Fibrin Split Products: Negative; Peripheral Blood Smear: Normal-sized platelets; Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with normal PT and platelet count strongly suggests a deficiency in the intrinsic pathway, likely Hemophilia A or B. To distinguish between them, I need to know your specific Factor VIII and Factor IX levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual; normal Factor VIII and IX levels with a prolonged PTT suggest an inhibitor or a different factor deficiency like Factor XI. Do you have a history of bleeding after other surgeries or dental work, and have you ever been tested for von Willebrand disease?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't had any other surgeries or dental work besides this extraction, so I don't know how I would bleed in those situations. I have never been tested for von Willebrand disease or any other specific bleeding disorders before.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the standard factors are normal, I need to rule out von Willebrand disease, which can sometimes present with a prolonged PTT. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal vWF and Factor VIII/IX levels, the prolonged PTT likely indicates a deficiency in Factor XI, XII, or the presence of an inhibitor. Do you have a family history of bleeding specifically after dental extractions or tonsillectomies, and have you ever experienced bleeding after minor cuts?

speaker: Patient
text: My uncle had similar bleeding problems and joint swelling, but I don't recall any specific issues with minor cuts in the past. I've never had a tonsillectomy or other surgeries, so I can't say how I would have bled in those situations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of joint swelling is a classic sign of hemarthrosis, which strongly points toward Hemophilia despite the confusing initial lab results. I need to check for a lupus anticoagulant or other inhibitors that might be artificially prolonging the PTT. REQUEST TEST: Mixing Study and Lupus Anticoagulant Screen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mixing Study: PTT corrects to normal upon mixing with normal plasma; Lupus Anticoagulant Screen: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the mixing study corrected the PTT, this confirms a factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor, and the normal Factor VIII/IX levels point toward Factor XI deficiency. Do you have a family history of bleeding specifically after dental extractions or tonsillectomies, and have you ever experienced bleeding after minor cuts?

speaker: Patient
text: My uncle had similar bleeding issues and joint swelling, but I don't recall any specific problems with minor cuts in the past. I've never had a tonsillectomy or other surgeries, so I can't say how I would have bled in those situations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The correction of the PTT in the mixing study confirms a factor deficiency, and since Factors VIII and IX are normal, Factor XI deficiency is the most likely cause given the dental bleeding history. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Level

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor XI level confirms the diagnosis of Hemophilia C, which aligns with your dental bleeding and family history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
